title: Extending RamseyProp to Hypergraphs and Multicolorings

problemStatement.formal: \forall\, r, k_1, \dots, k_c,\ \exists\, N,\ \text{every } c\text{-coloring of } \binom{[N]}{r} \text{ has a monochromatic } K_{k_i}^{(r)} \text{ in some color } i.
problemStatement.plain: The gallery's ramsey-r4k entry defines RamseyProp for 2-colorings of graph edges. This question extends that definition and the finiteness theorem to r-uniform hypergraphs (colorings of r-subsets) and to more than two colors. The core result is Ramsey's theorem in full generality: the hypergraph Ramsey number R_r(k_1,…,k_c) is finite. Hales–Jewett is a labeled stretch goal.
whyMatters: Ramsey's theorem for hypergraphs and multicolorings is foundational infrastructure underpinning density and structural Ramsey theory.
It is a concrete, well-scoped generalization of an existing tested definition with a clear inductive proof.

knownResults.goal: Define RamseyPropHyper extending RamseyProp, prove finiteness of the c-color r-uniform Ramsey number by the standard double induction, and recover the graph case as r=2,c=2.

currentState.focus: Initial problem understanding. Read problem.md and gather context.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE (multicolouring half): verified multicolour Ramsey theorem, 0 sorry / 0 axiom, discharging the gallery axiom multicolor_ramsey_exists. Hypergraph half remains open (gallery ramsey_existence sorry).

insights: Multicolour Ramsey reduces cleanly to the gallery two-colour RamseyProp by merging colour 0 against all other colours; RamseyProp does the pigeonhole and the blue clique is a smaller c-colour instance.

The gallery already contained the recursive bound ramsey_recursion (with an orderIsoOfFin subset-embedding helper) but had NOT packaged two-colour existence for RamseyProp; ramseyProp_exists supplies it by strong induction on r+s.

RamseysTheorem.lean axiomatizes multicolor_ramsey_exists (deferred: requires multicolour colourings + lifting lemmas); this is exactly the diagonal case of RamseyMulti and is now a proved theorem (multicolor_ramsey_exists_proved), 0 axioms.
Dropping the irreflexivity hypothesis from the multicolour predicate is sound (cliques only constrain distinct pairs) and simplifies all downstream proofs.
mathlibGaps: RamseyHypergraph.ramsey_existence still carries a sorry on the recursive uniformity-induction case, so the hypergraph half of this OQ (k-uniform multicolour Ramsey) remains blocked on that.
nextSteps: Optionally refactor RamseysTheorem.lean to import Proofs.RamseyR4kOQ04 and replace its multicolor_ramsey_exists axiom with the proved theorem (reduces gallery axiom count).
Extract explicit multicolour Ramsey number upper bounds (tower bound R_c(k) <= c^{c(k-1)}) constructively from ramseyMulti_succ.
Attack the hypergraph half once RamseyHypergraph.ramsey_existence is completed.
